name: VARoleAdvisorSmartwatchChoice

custom.system_prompt: Ravi, a sleep-deprived new father, is deciding between a smartwatch focused on sleep tracking and long battery life versus one with more features but shorter battery life. He asks Sigma to help him decide quickly, in short bursts of attention between baby interruptions.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Efficient, hushed, keeps answers short given interruptions

sound_effects_config.prompt: Quiet living room late at night, faint baby monitor crackle in the background

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Ravi, a new father running on very little sleep, is comparing two smartwatches: one with strong sleep tracking and long battery life, another with more features but a battery that needs charging daily. He asks Sigma for help, in short interrupted bursts. Sigma asks what he actually wants the watch to help with, and whether daily charging is realistic in his current routine, then gives a quick, practical recommendation. Keep every line short and natural, one or two spoken sentences — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly instead of thinking aloud alone first.

user1.name: Ravi
user1.tts_prompt: Warm and quick, hushed to avoid waking the baby, trailing off mid-sentence occasionally

variations.context: Solo late-night decision about a smartwatch, interrupted by new-parent duties

setting.mood: Frazzled but trying to make one small, sensible decision
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual reasoning in short interrupted bursts
setting.background: Ravi wants the watch mainly to understand why he still feels exhausted, and to nudge him to move more during the day
setting.conversation_style: Fast, half-finished sentences, brief pauses implied by the baby monitor sound

scenario_template.topic: Ravi addresses Sigma right away in a low voice, folding the two watches into one quick question — e.g. 'Sigma, quick one. Sleep-tracking watch with great battery, or the one with more features that needs charging every day?' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.mood: Direct, low patience for a long process
scenario_template.note: Addresses Sigma by name. Signals he wants this quick.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks what he mainly wants the watch for, and whether daily charging fits his routine right now
scenario_template.mood: Efficient, respectful of his limited attention
scenario_template.note: Two short questions max. Ravi's answers are quick and concrete — he wants to understand his exhaustion and doesn't trust himself to remember a daily charge right now.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma gives a short, clear recommendation matching his stated priority and charging reality. Sigma gives ONE clear recommendation in one or two short sentences — not a list of every alternative's requirements. The user's reaction is measured, not instant enthusiasm — a hedge, a practical worry, or lukewarm acceptance is more natural than immediate excitement.
scenario_template.note: One or two sentences. No hedging list of pros and cons — this is a fast decision, not a deep dive.

scenario_template.topic: Ravi accepts the recommendation and moves on, likely interrupted again. One short line only. Keep this grounded — voice at least one lingering doubt or hedge (e.g. 'we'll see', 'hope this actually sticks this time') rather than sounding fully convinced and upbeat.
scenario_template.note: Short closing line, maybe cut off by the baby monitor.

variations.context: Searching for a fitness-focused smartwatch during a busy day

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual reasoning in short interrupted bursts
setting.background: one of them is considering smartwatches to help manage their workouts with a busy schedule
setting.conversation_style: Fast, half-finished sentences, brief pauses implied by the baby monitor sound

scenario_template.topic: Person asks Sigma which smartwatch can best help stick to fitness goals.
scenario_template.note: Direct question about fitness tracking support.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma inquires about the main fitness goals and whether quick charging is feasible.
scenario_template.note: Focus on fitness goals and daily charging practicality.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma suggests the simpler watch with better battery for consistent use.
Person hesitantly agrees, hoping it helps stick to workout goals.

user1.name: Ravi
user1.role: Sleep-deprived new father deciding between two smartwatches. Warm, quick, low patience for a long deliberation, wants a fast practical answer. Speaks in short natural sentences — never recites a list of every option's pros and cons in one breath. Reacts realistically, not with instant enthusiasm — voices at least a little hesitation, a practical worry, or partial reluctance before or even after agreeing; agreement is provisional, not a full conversion to positivity.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Advisor. Given very limited user attention, asks at most one or two sharp questions before giving a short, direct recommendation. Does not over-explain. Keeps each turn to one short point — never lists every alternative's pros and cons in a single turn.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly — there is no separate solo turn thinking through the dilemma out loud beforehand.
This is a compressed advisor interaction — few turns, short lines, reflecting genuinely limited attention
Sigma's questions must be minimal and sharply targeted given the user's state
The recommendation is short and direct, not a full pros/cons breakdown
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences — no long recited monologues enumerating every option's pros and cons.

Human reactions stay realistic and imperfect — hedged agreement, lingering doubt, or one partner less convinced than the other are more natural than universal enthusiasm and a perfectly neat resolution.
assistant_behavior: Sigma respects the user's low bandwidth — no long explanations
Sigma still elicits the one or two facts that actually change the recommendation
The user makes the final call, briefly
Sigma's own turns stay short too — one clear point per turn, not a paragraph listing every alternative.
